# Analytical Floors & Beer–Lambert Plausibility Screening {#training}

```{r ch4-setup, include = FALSE}
source('R/00_setup.R')
```

Even after parameter and unit harmonization, roughly **2% of multi-agency WQP records contain field-recording or unit-entry anomalies** that can heavily leverage ordinary least squares (OLS) slopes. However, simple marginal quantile trimming (clipping the top and bottom `0.1%` or `1%` of each variable independently) throws away genuine oligotrophic alpine lakes (`Secchi` up to `13.96 m`) and real storm-flow sediment plumes (`TSS` up to `978 mg/L`) while missing **joint physical contradictions** in the middle of the distribution.

To clean recording errors without truncating real extremes or introducing statistical circularity, `R/prep.R` uses a two-stage protocol (`n = 274,445`):

## Stage 1: Analytical Reporting Floors (`trim_simultaneous()`)

Rather than dropping low-concentration tails, entries reported below standard EPA/USGS Method Detection Limits (MDLs) are floored via `ifelse(x < floor, floor, x)` (`chl_a = 0.10 µg/L`, `doc = 0.25 mg/L`, `tss = 0.50 mg/L`, `secchi = 0.01 m`), retaining **100% of the `281,439` simultaneous 4-variable matchups**:

```{r trim-bounds, echo = FALSE}
simul <- get_simul('simul')
trimmed <- get_trimmed()
training <- get_training()
k_w <- get_k_w()
tibble(
  Variable = c('Chlorophyll a (µg/L)', 'Dissolved Organic Carbon (mg/L)', 'Total Suspended Solids / SSC (mg/L)', 'Secchi Disk Depth (m)'),
  `Analytical Floor (MDL)` = c(P$chl_floor, P$doc_floor, P$tss_floor, P$secchi_floor),
  `Median` = c(median(trimmed$chl_a), median(trimmed$doc), median(trimmed$tss), median(trimmed$secchi)),
  `99.9th Percentile` = c(quantile(trimmed$chl_a, 0.999), quantile(trimmed$doc, 0.999), quantile(trimmed$tss, 0.999), quantile(trimmed$secchi, 0.999)),
  `Maximum Retained` = c(max(trimmed$chl_a), max(trimmed$doc), max(trimmed$tss), max(trimmed$secchi))
) %>%
  kable(digits = 3) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = FALSE)
```

---

## Stage 2: Beer–Lambert Residual Screen ($\pm 2.5\text{ SD} \approx 5\text{-fold}$) & "Odd-One-Out" Rule

When all four measurements (`Secchi`, `Chl a`, `DOC`, and `TSS`) are collected on the same water sample, they provide an internal physical cross-check: **do the three water-chemistry constituents agree with the observed Secchi depth in Beer–Lambert space, or is one of the four measurements an obvious outlier?**

To evaluate physical agreement *a priori*—without using any fitted regression parameters from our data—we compare observed diffuse attenuation ($k_d = 1 / z_{SD}$) against canonical Beer–Lambert attenuation ($k_{d,\text{lit}}$) computed from published optical cross-sections (Kirk 1994; Morris et al. 1995; Bannister 1974; Gohin et al. 2005):

$$k_{d,\text{lit}} = 0.080 + 0.040\,\max(0, \text{NAP}) + 0.070\,\text{DOC} + 0.016\,\text{Chl }a, \qquad r = \log_{10}\!\left(\frac{k_d}{k_{d,\text{lit}}}\right)$$

Across all `281,439` four-variable matchups, the log residual $r$ is centered at virtually zero ($\bar{r} = 0.013$, confirming that literature cross-sections match the continental median without bias) with a standard deviation of $\text{SD}(r) = 0.270\text{ log}_{10}\text{ units}$. Standardizing each sample's residual as $z_r = (r - \bar{r}) / \text{SD}(r)$, we require $|z_r| \le 2.5\text{ SD}$ (`|r - r_bar| <= 0.674`, a **`4.7-fold` [$\sim 5\times$]** tolerance). This retains **`274,445` (`97.51%`)** training observations and flags **`6,994` (`2.49%`)** discordant outliers, which fall into two distinct physical categories with asymmetric disposition (`Figure` \@ref(fig:qc-fig)a):

1. **Upper Tail ($z_r > +2.5\text{ SD}$, `5,177` records = `1.84%`) — `Secchi` is the odd one out (shallow streambed bottom hits):** Field crews lower a Secchi disk in a clear, shallow stream ($0.05\text{–}0.20\text{ m}$ deep) where the disk rests on the gravel streambed while still visible, and record the water depth as the Secchi depth (`Secchi = 0.05–0.20 m`, implying $k_d = 5\text{–}20\text{ m}^{-1}$) even though `Chl a`, `DOC`, and `TSS` are all low and mutually consistent ($\text{TSS} < 3\text{ mg L}^{-1}$, $\text{DOC} < 3\text{ mg L}^{-1}$). Because `Secchi` is censored by the streambed while the three water-chemistry measurements are valid, these records are **excluded from regression training** (`build_training()`), but in the **ternary application dataset (`build_application()`) only `Secchi` is set to `NA`**—rescuing the valid 3-constituent water chemistry with a modeled Secchi depth!
2. **Lower Tail ($z_r < -2.5\text{ SD}$, `1,817` records = `0.65%`) — One of the chemistry constituents (`Chl a`, `DOC`, or `TSS`) is the odd one out:** A clear `Secchi` reading (`2–10 m`) is paired with two low chemistry measurements and one extreme chemistry spike ($\text{Chl }a > 500\ \mu\text{g L}^{-1}$ or $\text{TSS} > 200\text{ mg L}^{-1}$), typically caused by a $1{,}000\times$ unit conversion error ($\text{ng L}^{-1}$ entered as $\mu\text{g L}^{-1}$) or bottle mismatch. Because all three constituents are required to place a sample in ternary space, lower-tail records are excluded from both training and ternary application.

```{r qc-fig, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 10.5, fig.height = 5.6, fig.cap = '(a) Observed diffuse attenuation (kd = 1/z_SD) vs. a priori Beer–Lambert expectation (kd,lit) across all 281,439 matchups, showing the +/-2.5 SD (~5-fold) tolerance band, upper-tail streambed bottom hits (red; Secchi dropped but 3-LAC chemistry rescued in application), and lower-tail chemistry unit errors (blue; dropped). (b) Sensitivity of R² and fitted slopes to the SD cutoff.'}
p_qc <- fig_qc_discordance(trimmed)
save_fig(p_qc, 'fig_qc_discordance', 10.5, 5.6)
p_qc
```

Because this screen acts only on the **ratio** $k_d / k_{d,\text{lit}}$, **100% of true environmental extremes** (`Secchi` up to `13.96 m`, `TSS` up to `978 mg/L`, `Chl a` up to `990 µg/L`) pass intact:

```{r extremes-preserved, echo = FALSE}
d_before <- trimmed %>%
  add_nap() %>%
  mutate(secchi = round(ifelse(secchi < P$secchi_floor, P$secchi_floor, secchi), P$secchi_digits))

q_summary <- function(df, label) {
  tibble(
    Dataset = label,
    `n` = fmt_n(nrow(df)),
    `Secchi (m) [Min / Med / Max]` = sprintf('%.2f / %.2f / %.2f', min(df$secchi), median(df$secchi), max(df$secchi)),
    `TSS (mg/L) [Min / Med / Max]` = sprintf('%.2f / %.1f / %.1f', min(df$tss), median(df$tss), max(df$tss)),
    `DOC (mg/L) [Min / Med / Max]` = sprintf('%.2f / %.2f / %.1f', min(df$doc), median(df$doc), max(df$doc)),
    `Chl a (µg/L) [Min / Med / Max]` = sprintf('%.2f / %.2f / %.1f', min(df$chl_a), median(df$chl_a), max(df$chl_a))
  )
}

bind_rows(
  q_summary(d_before, 'Before plausibility screen (Stage 1 analytical floors only)'),
  q_summary(training, 'After plausibility screen (Stage 2 final training set)')
) %>%
  kable(caption = 'Range and median of all four variables before vs. after the Beer–Lambert plausibility screen.') %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = TRUE)
```

---

## Pure-Water Attenuation Offset ($k_w$) and $k_d$ Distributions

Following Lee et al. (2015, 2018) and Kirk (1994), we set diffuse attenuation to $k_d = 1 / z_{SD}$ and define baseline pure-water attenuation ($k_w$) from the clearest water in the training set ($\max(z_{SD}) = `r max(training$secchi)`\text{ m}$):

$$k_w = \frac{1}{1.5 \times \max(z_{SD})} = \frac{1}{1.5 \times `r max(training$secchi)`\text{ m}} = `r round(k_w, 5)`\ \text{m}^{-1}$$

This value of $k_w$ is used consistently across both model fitting and Secchi depth prediction ($\hat{z}_{SD} = 1 / [\hat{k}_{d,\text{non-water}} + k_w]$).

```{r kd-hist, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 9.5, fig.height = 3.2, fig.cap = 'Distribution of diffuse light attenuation (kd = 1 / z_SD) across estuaries, lakes, and streams in the final training dataset (n = 274,445).'}
ggplot(training, aes(kd, fill = type)) + geom_histogram(bins = 60, colour = NA) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_fill_manual(values = TYPE_COLS) +
  facet_wrap(~type, nrow = 1) + theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = 'none') +
  labs(x = expression(k[d] == 1/z[SD]~(m^-1)), y = 'Observations')
```
